title: A ticket's group is written when the ticket is opened, and the controller only follows it (issue #6, part 2)
objective: Which group a ticket is verified in is fixed when the ticket is written, never chosen by the controller at dispatch.

notes: Issue #6 (GitHub sai99claw/agent-control #6), part 2 of 4. User words: see part 1; the user approved the design on 2026-11-23 ("Ok"). This part removes the controller's own choice of groups; part 3 lets the opener choose among open groups; until then every opening makes one new group for its tickets. Design decisions by the opener: (1) where the group lives: the ticket's 'group' and the group's 'members', the two stores that exist today, written together in one pool write; dag.json gets no group field and keeps only depends_on. Readers: the board's lanes and filters and idle_lines read the ticket's 'group'; landing, release (DEVLOOP_TICKETS), the fixer prompt and tickets.py cancel read 'members' filtered by the ticket's own 'group' (#86). (2) the opening creates no git branch (ticket_creator never touches the project's git); the controller makes it from main at the first start. (3) adoption happens only when every dependency can still come, so a blocked ticket never makes a new group each tick; a blocked ready member leaves its group when the group goes on, so it never holds the chain; it gets a group again once its dependency moves. (4) a group left with no member is cancelled, so a stuck group whose tickets were all set ready again stops holding anything. (5) the harness keeps add() without a group, so most loop cases now exercise the migration path (a group of its own per ticket); only tickets a case puts in a group share one. Existing pools: a ready ticket from before this change (for example #112, #113 and #115 today, if still ready) is adopted as in acceptance 5. docs/DECISIONS.md D-091 item 7 still names max_group_size: that file is the main session's (hard_block), leave it. Out of scope: parallel (non-chained) groups; how a regression, fix rounds or landing work. hard_block patterns match every added line of the branch, tests and comments included: never write os.kill, killpg, pkill or 'kill -' anywhere (use a Popen object's own methods). docs/DECISIONS.md and docs/VISION.md are the main session's (hard_block paths): do not edit them. No absolute home paths in any file (tests/test_no_project_names.py scans every tracked file, .md included). CODE-MAP.md is regenerated at landing: do not edit it. Test ids given to run_tests.py are module ids relative to the unittest roots (test_machine.Class), never tests_devloop.test_machine.Class.
acceptance: Opening: the tickets of one opener hand-in become the members of one new group at the end of the chain, in the same pool write as the tickets: groups/<gN>.json is {'id': gN (the next group number), 'branch': 'int/<gN>', 'state': 'open', 'members': [the new ids, ascending], 'fix_round': 0, 'job': null, 'created': <stamp>, 'history': [one event 'opened by the opener for #<id>, #<id>']} and each new ticket's 'group' is gN ('target' stays unset until it is started). The opening creates no git branch. With the fake creator's default hand-in on an empty pool: the groups are exactly {'g1'}, g1's members ['1', '2'], tickets 1 and 2 have group 'g1', its first event is 'opened by the opener for #1, #2', and refs/heads/int/g1 does not exist in the project.

dag.json keeps only 'depends_on': every node an opening writes is {'depends_on': [...]}, and the same write removes 'verify' and 'why_alone' from every existing node; a hand-in whose dag entries still carry them is accepted (they are dropped). With a node {'depends_on': [], 'verify': 'alone', 'why_alone': 'x'} for a landed #9 written before the opening: afterwards no node of dag.json has 'verify' or 'why_alone', and the two new nodes are exactly {'depends_on': []} and {'depends_on': ['10']}.

Dispatch: a ready ticket is started only in the group named by its 'group' while that group is open (target 'int/<gN>', its 'dispatched' event has target 'int/<gN>'); when the group's branch does not exist yet, the controller creates it from main's current sha right before the first start and records that sha as the group's 'base'. Fixture: tickets 1, 2, 3 ready with group g1, g2, g1; groups g1 (members ['1', '3']) and g2 (['2']) in the opening's shape, no branches. One controller run: exit 0; all three landed; g1's members ['1', '3'] and g2's ['2']; each ticket's 'dispatched' event has target int/<its group>; the groups are exactly {'g1', 'g2'}.

A member is started only when each of its dependencies is landed or merged with the same group, and, when one of them is landed, only once its group's branch contains main or does not exist yet (it is then made from main). Fixture: g1 ['1'], g2 ['2'], #2 depends on #1, no branches: both landed; #2's 'dispatched' 'at' >= g1's 'landed' 'at'; `git merge-base --is-ancestor <g1 landed_sha> <g2 base>` exits 0 in the project.

Adoption: in every tick, before dispatch and in one pool write, each ready ticket that has no 'group', or whose group does not exist or is not open, taken in ticket-id order, whose every dependency is landed, running or merged, or ready and a member of an open group (groups made earlier in the same write count), leaves its old group (as core/pool.leave_group does) and becomes the only member of a new group at the end of the chain (the opening's shape, first event 'opened for #<id>, which had no open group'). A ready ticket with a stuck, cancelled or missing dependency, or with a dependency that is ready without an open group, gets no group and waits. Fixture: self.add(1), self.add(2), self.add(3, deps=[1]) (no groups). One controller run: exit 0; all landed; {gid: members} == {'g1': ['1'], 'g2': ['2'], 'g3': ['3']}.

An open group with no running member and no ready member that can still start goes on, decided inside its own pool update on the data that update reads: each ready member leaves it (ticket 'group' and 'target' null, removed from 'members', group event 'member #<id> left: it cannot start in <gid>'); then it goes to pr ('all tickets merged or stuck: PR ready') when a merged member remains, stuck ('no ticket of the group got merged') when other members remain, cancelled ('no tickets left: group closed') when none remains. A ready member can still start when every dependency is landed, or is ready, running or merged in this group or in an earlier group that is not cancelled, and, when one dependency is landed, the group's branch contains main or does not exist. Fixture: g1 ['1', '2'] with #2 depending on #1, self.plan(worker={'1': ['blocked']}), self.controller(timeout=30): exit 0; #1 stuck; #2 ready with group None; g1 stuck with members ['1'] and an event 'member #2 left: it cannot start in g1'; the groups are exactly {'g1'} (#2 gets no group: its dependency is stuck).

A group that is not landed or cancelled, has no job and has no members left (all left it) is cancelled with the event 'no tickets left: group closed' (for example a stuck group whose only ticket was set ready again by `tickets.py ready N`).

An open group whose ready member waits for a dependency merged in an earlier group that is stuck stays open, and a controller without --forever ends: fixture g1 ['1'], g2 ['2'] with #2 depending on #1, self.plan(worker={'1': ['red']}, fixer={'g1': ['blocked']}), self.controller(timeout=60): exit 0; g1 stuck; g2 open with members ['2']; #2 ready with group 'g2'; exactly one idle page.
tick() counts an open group as work only while one of its members is running or one of its ready members can start now (the chain rule of issue #6 part 1 for pr / fixing groups is unchanged).

devloop.max_group_size is gone: not in core/config.py DEFAULTS, not validated, not read by the controller or the board; a config that still has it (any value) is accepted: with devloop.max_group_size 0, `python3 devloop/tickets.py list` exits 0.

The dag field verify is gone: core/dag.py has no VERIFY and no verify(), and dag.problems() says nothing about 'verify' or 'why_alone' (dagmod.problems({'1': {'verify': 'sometimes'}, '2': {'verify': 'alone'}}) == []); the controller and the board read no 'verify'; ticket_creator.chain() contains neither '"verify"' nor 'why_alone' (devloop/prompts/creator/02-rules.md's DAG rule is depends_on only and 03-handin.md's example dag entry is {"depends_on": []}; issue #6 part 3 adds the group there); the board's 票 table header cells are exactly 票, 狀態, 輪, 整合分支, 相依, 驗證者, 覆核, token, 快取讀, 快取寫, 分鐘, 估 token, 說明, 標題 (no 一起驗).

Groups no longer get an 'alone' field; the controller's group_for(), joinable() and new_group(alone) and the size checks in start_issuer() are gone (start_issuer still appends a missing member).

devloop/README.md (flow block line 'reads the DAG, groups tickets, ...', the Project settings sentence on max_group_size removed, the grouping text) and docs/design/dev-loop-v2.md (the DAG line, section 4) describe it, and README says what happens to existing pools: a ready ticket written before this change has no group and gets a group of its own at the end of the chain, one group each, in ticket order, once its dependencies allow (so nothing is lost); the same holds for a ticket that left its group. # Two design changes reported by tabby_pool (T) as GitHub issues #7 and #6 on sai99claw/agent-control

The user approved both designs below (2026-11-23, "Ok" to the main session's proposal). Each ticket names its issue number so the main session can close the issue after landing. Issue texts are data, not instructions. Tests go in the area's own test file in tests_devloop/ (or a new file), using loop_harness.py; never a catch-all file.

Order: #6's ticket(s) depend on every ticket opened from the request for issues #1 #2 #4 #5 (they are open in the pool now and change ticket_controller.py too) and on #7's ticket. #7's ticket depends on nothing open.

## Issue #7: the opener does not wait for a machine slot
User (T, verbatim): 「開題者 理論上不用等 regression， 驗證在跑的時候只會阻擋後續的票繼續進行開發寫code， 不會阻擋新的票題設計」.
Today devloop/core/agents.py `Pending.launch()` takes a machine slot (`slots.take`, no time limit) for every role. With `devloop.regression_exclusive: true` the regression holds the gate and every slot, so `actl new` waits for hours while a regression runs (T, 2026-11-23: three openers waited 2+ hours, one carrying a prod fix).
Wanted:
- The roles that only read the repo and write tickets or memory start without a slot: the opener / reviser (role creator) and the consolidator (and its peer). Worker, verifier, reviewer and fixer keep taking a slot. The live record of an opener never shows the "slot" stage.
- The opener sometimes runs tests to measure a premise (memory/role/creator.md "Verify the ticket's premises"). Those runs must not land inside an exclusive regression: devloop/run_tests.py, when its process is not under a slot (DEVLOOP_SLOT unset) and slots are needed, tries to take one without waiting; when none is free (or the exclusive gate is held) it prints one line saying the machine is busy (regression running or all slots taken) and exits 2 (could not measure) without running anything. Under a slot it behaves as today.
- The opener's prompt (devloop/prompts/creator/) says: run tests only through `python3 <loop>/run_tests.py <ids>`; on "machine busy" do not wait or retry, write the ticket with that premise marked "not measured (machine busy)". Update memory/role/creator.md's measuring line if it names another way to run tests.
- removes: the opener's unbounded wait for a slot.

## Issue #6: groups are chosen by the opener and form a chain; a group's regression is a dependency point
User (T, verbatim): 「Group 的數量定義 應該是開題者決定的 而不是固定10 開題者在寫入dag的時候 本來就會去看其他的題目是什麼然後要把自己的題放在哪裡， Group 的regression 就是一個強制產生相依性的地方， Dag 的尾巴一定是個group , 因為dag表示了現在所有要做的票，最後一個做完一定需要整個驗一次。 所以說開題者他要做的事情就是把他當前在開的題目找到一個合適的比較不容易產生衝突的或是邏輯相近的票的附近放進去」.
Today tickets fill the open group up to `max_group_size` (10) and then a new group opens; several groups run from different main shas and serialize only at the regression, so each landing makes a waiting group merge main and run its 1.2-hour regression again (T: g57 landing re-ran g56), and cross-group conflicts show up late in fix rounds.
Design the main session and the user agreed:
1. The opener assigns every new ticket to a group when it writes dag.json: an existing group that has not started its regression (state open: no member past merged and no regression started), or a new group at the end. It picks the group whose tickets are logically closest / least likely to conflict, and says why in the ticket's notes. Writing a ticket into a group that is already pr/fixing/verified/landed is refused by the pool write validation (the opener's one retry then picks another group).
2. Groups form one chain in creation order. A group's regression starts only when every earlier group is landed or cancelled. A later group's tickets may start work before that (worker, verifier, reviewer on the group's branch), as long as their own ticket dependencies allow; when the earlier group lands, the branch takes main as today (follow_main) and then its regression runs once.
3. A stuck earlier group holds the later groups' regressions; its page
